parent: LloydsPharmacy (online doctor business; ownership not checked in this stage)
model: UK online pharmacy and doctor service (Shopify shop front plus a server-driven questionnaire engine) selling licensed and off-label prescription hair-loss medicines to men.

access.accountWall: No sign-in is needed for the questions or the recommendation. "Continue as a new patient" (…/clinic/hair-loss?guest) starts as a guest. After the recommendation, choosing a product, the pack size (Add to basket) and a finasteride safety screen, the last screen is "Please confirm the following to complete your consultation" (question 100467, "I confirm the above"). The walk stopped there and did not press it, so the exact sign-in point (expected straight after it) was not seen.
blockers: A "This service operates in the United Kingdom only" pop-up (closed with "Continue with UK service"); not bot protection.
The engine is server-driven: the full question set is not in the browser code, so branches were mapped by walking.
Some checklist options open explanation pop-ups or could not be clicked by the walker (Phaeochromocytoma onwards in the conditions list, two medicines options, the previous-treatment list).
access.coverageNote: Stage 1 walked every question on the baseline path and every option one level deep. Stage 2 (24 Nov 2026) replayed the baseline and ran 33 one-change experiments to the recommendation screen, comparing cards and wording (runs/e01 to runs/e33). Options not replayed are marked unknown or inferred. Stage 3 (24 Nov 2026) replayed the baseline and 8 key rules (all confirmed) and filled 7 gaps (phaeochromocytoma, porphyria, SLE, scalp creams, eGFR not tested, testosterone, and one two-change combination); see verification.

products.name: Finasteride tablets (generic)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for male pattern hair loss
products.priceDetail: Subscription (pack-size screen in the consultation): £28.00 a month, £80.00 every 3 months, £138.00 every 6 months ("Save 15% & cancel anytime"). Recommendation card shows "From £6.79 a week".
products.recommendedWhen: Offered unless any finasteride exclusion is given: trying for a baby, breast cancer, breast tissue enlargement, prostate cancer, problems with sex life, 5-ARI for prostate, ED tablets, finasteride allergy, depression opt-out, or past finasteride side effects with "No" to trying again. The only drug left for heart/BP, BP medicines or minoxidil allergy. Named in the "licensed first" advice for new patients (observed).

products.name: Propecia (branded finasteride)
products.priceDetail: Card shows "From £8.75 a week". Subscription prices not captured.
products.recommendedWhen: Same rules as generic finasteride; always listed under "Other suitable treatments" next to it (observed).

products.name: Sons Minoxidil spray
products.legalStatus: P medicine (minoxidil 5% topical; inferred from UK status of 5% minoxidil solutions)
products.recommendedWhen: Offered unless scalp changes, medicated scalp creams, heart/BP condition, BP medicines or minoxidil allergy. The only product left for men on ED tablets. Named in the "licensed first" advice (observed).

products.name: Hair loss tablets (oral minoxidil)
products.legalStatus: POM used off-label (minoxidil tablets are licensed for high blood pressure, not hair loss)
products.recommendedWhen: Offered unless age 65 or over, kidney disease (eGFR over 30, unknown or not tested), phaeochromocytoma, porphyria, SLE, heart/BP condition, BP medicines, ED tablets or minoxidil allergy (observed).

products.priceDetail: Card: "From £7.35 a week", "94% experience an improvement in hair loss". On 23 Nov 2026 the card data said inStock false.
products.recommendedWhen: Shown first whenever both finasteride and topical minoxidil are allowed (no exclusion for either); flagged out of stock on 24 Nov 2026 (observed).

products.priceDetail: Card: "From £7.35 a week"; "We recommend as an oral alternative to the classic combo". inStock false on 23 Nov 2026.

flows.name: Hair loss consultation (men only; one flow for every entry point)
flows.stagesSummary: Login prompt (Continue as a new patient) → "Before we begin" + "I confirm the above" → sex at birth → date of birth → education (optional, 3 screens) → 4 hair-loss questions → previous treatment (per product: helped? duration, adherence, side effects, retry finasteride?) → conditions → kidney → heart/BP → other conditions → medicines → allergies → partner pregnancy → pets → results info → answers summary → recommendation cards → pack size → finasteride safety → final consent (walk stops here; account expected next).
entryPoints: https://core.onlinedoctor.lloydspharmacy.com/api/questionnaire/products/3756 (collection page top button; 3756 is the clinic default SKU)

questions.text: What causes hair loss?: Male pattern hair loss is caused by a combination of genetics and sensitivity to DHT (dihydrotestosterone) , a hormone made from testosterone. In people who are susceptible, DHT gradually causes affected hair follicles to shrink and shortens the hair growth phase. New hairs become finer and shorter and may eventually stop growing in some areas of the scalp. Treatments can help slow further hair loss and may support regrowth. Options include finasteride and minoxidil , which work in different ways.
questions.purpose: Education: what causes male pattern hair loss.

questions.text: How does finasteride work?: Finasteride reduces DHT by blocking an enzyme that converts testosterone into DHT. Lowering DHT can slow the shrinking of affected hair follicles. When taken consistently, finasteride can slow hair loss and may support regrowth in some men.
questions.purpose: Education: how finasteride works.

questions.text: How does minoxidil work?: Minoxidil increases blood flow and nutrients to hair roots. Used regularly, it can help hair grow back thicker over time. It usually takes a few months to notice a difference. Some men use finasteride and minoxidil together. Complete your assessment to find out what's right for you.
questions.purpose: Education: how minoxidil works.

questions.text: Steroids are thought to create male pattern hair loss by causing your body to produce higher levels of dihydrotestosterone (DHT). DHT acts on the hair follicles on your scalp, causing them to weaken over time. They eventually die and stop growing back, which results in baldness. Taking Finasteride or Propecia is unlikely to be helpful if you are still taking steroids. Steroids can also cause lots of other problems such as erectile dysfunction, infertility, heart and kidney problems as well as mood disorders.

Oral tablets or capsules are less likely to pose a risk because the medication does not sit on your hair or skin in the same way. However, tablets or capsules are still harmful if a pet ingests them. engineSummary: A server-side rules engine (one screen per answer) works as a subtraction filter. It starts from six cards for every eligible man (two combination packs, generic finasteride, oral minoxidil, Sons minoxidil spray, Propecia) and removes whole drug families: any finasteride exclusion (baby plans, breast or prostate cancer, breast tissue enlargement, sex-life problems, 5-ARI or ED medicines, allergy, mood opt-out, past side effects declined) drops every finasteride product; heart/BP disease, BP medicines or minoxidil allergy drop every minoxidil product, even the spray; age 65+, kidney disease, phaeochromocytoma, porphyria, SLE or ED tablets drop oral minoxidil; scalp changes or medicated scalp creams drop topicals. When both families are gone, the questions end early with no product. Hard stops end the questions for women, under-18s, non-pattern loss and severe kidney or liver disease. Answers never change strength, dose, plan or price, and never add a product: history and efficacy answers only change the result wording. Follow-up questions are skipped once the drug they protect is gone.
strengths: Free, anonymous route to a named-clinician recommendation with prices before any account.
Clear, consistent safety logic: removes whole drug families for real contraindications (heart/BP, ED tablets with oral minoxidil, age 65+, kidney disease, 5-ARI use).
Smart skipping: pets and pregnancy questions disappear once the drug they relate to is off the table, so the patient is not asked irrelevant questions.
Takes a proper treatment history: benefit, duration, adherence and side effects for each previous product, and lets the patient choose to retry finasteride after side effects.
Mental-health screen with a finasteride opt-out and crisis signposting; expectation-setting for temple-only and extensive loss.
weaknesses: Men only: women are stopped after one question.
Several removals are silent: breast or prostate cancer, sex-life problems, heart/BP, age 65+ and kidney disease change the offer with no screen explaining why.

Blunt rules: a heart or BP condition (even treated, mild hypertension) removes the minoxidil spray as well as tablets; "problems with my sex life" removes finasteride outright instead of discussing it.

No personalisation of strength, dose or plan: one 1 mg finasteride, one minoxidil tablet strength, one 5% spray. A failed product is still offered with only a wording change; no stronger or alternative option (e.g. compounded or dutasteride) exists.
Combination packs lead the result screen while flagged out of stock.
No questions on goals, how far the loss has progressed over time, family history, diet, stress, thyroid or iron, or photos before the recommendation.
opportunities: Products for men excluded from both drugs (e.g. heart/BP plus finasteride exclusion) currently get nothing: offer non-drug or cosmetic routes and GP signposting.
Strength and format choice: low-dose oral minoxidil titration, foam for sensitive scalps, topical finasteride, or a step-up for non-responders.
Explain every removal on the result screen and give a next step, which Lloyds does not do for its silent exclusions.
In-stock combination packs: Lloyds leads with combinations it cannot supply.
limitations: Only the anonymous part of the flow was tested; the final consent (100467) was not pressed, so the exact sign-in point and the clinician review step are unseen.

Untested options are marked unknown or inferred: two liver sub-options, previous oral minoxidil / other medication, "too early to tell", "less than 12 months", irregular use, 108419 Yes, the minor medicines in 108158, Guanethidine and obstructive uropathy to the end.
Only one combination of answers was replayed (heart/BP plus prostate cancer). Other combinations are assumed to follow the same subtraction logic (inferred).
Pack size and safety screens were only walked for finasteride; plan prices for other products come from the product data, not a walk.
Free-text answers were neutral; a clinician may act on them after submission, which cannot be seen.
FAQ, help-centre and subscription-terms pages were not read. Legal status of the minoxidil sprays is inferred.
Stock flags (both Dual Action packs out of stock) and prices were checked on 24 Nov 2026 and can change.

verification.verdict: High trust for what it covers. All 8 high-impact rules re-tested live in stage 3 gave exactly the recorded result: heart/BP removes every minoxidil product, age 65 removes oral minoxidil, ED tablets leave only the spray, trying for a baby and prostate cancer remove every finasteride product, and female, sudden onset and eGFR under 30 end the questions. The baseline replay matched card for card, and all 7 product prices and strengths match the live pages. No rule was contradicted; one wording error was fixed (a woman is still asked her date of birth), and seven gaps were filled, all fitting the same subtraction engine. The weak points are what was never seen: the account wall after the final consent, a few rare options, and answer combinations other than the one tested.
